key_insight: A genomic foundation model (Evo2) extracted from tumor sequence alterations added prognostic value beyond established clinicopathologic and transcriptomic risk models in soft tissue sarcoma.
clinical_relevance: If validated prospectively, sequence-context genomic features could help refine survival risk stratification alongside SARCULATOR and CINSARC in sarcoma care.
method: Used FFPE tumor samples and clinical data from 102 patients with dedifferentiated liposarcoma, high-grade leiomyosarcoma, or undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma.
Converted reconstructable short variants, fusions, and rearrangements into sequence inputs, embedded them with Evo2, and aggregated patient-level genomic representations.
Tested Cox survival models for OS, PFS, DFS, RFS, and MFS, with external validation in TCGA-SARC (n = 129).
evidence_signal: Descriptive C-index comparisons showed improved discrimination when Evo2 was added to SARCULATOR or CINSARC, and Evo2 alone outperformed either model alone in TCGA-SARC.
watch_item: These are point-estimate comparisons from retrospective cohorts, so prospective validation and assessment of real-world implementation are still needed.
paper_title: Genomic foundation models extend clinicopathologic and transcriptomic prognostication in soft tissue sarcoma
